params.message:
Communities: name KUBO CyberSec, give it a page with its first event

/communities now lists its first community, KUBO CyberSec in The Gambia, with a link
to its own page, and keeps a card open for the clubs to come. The "Soon" label is gone.

The new page /communities/cybersec (with nl and fr copies) says what the community is,
who it is for and how to join, and shows its first event, a Capture the Flag on
Saturday 14 November 2026, with the facts from the poster, the poster itself (webp at
848 and 480 px, explicit dimensions, descriptive alt text, a JPG to download), the
community's sudo ./learn keycap sticker in the header, and how to register. It carries
schema.org Event data.

The contact number for registration is kept out of reach of scrapers. It is not in
the source or the built site as digits: the page holds an encoded form
(src/lib/contact.js) and a "Show number" button decodes it in the browser on click;
without JS the box points to info@kubo.global. The served poster copies have the
number painted out in the poster's own background, and the alt text refers to the
page instead. A check over the built site (npm run check:built, now a CI step after
the build) fails if any form of the number appears in a page, script, sitemap or
other text file the site serves; unit tests cover the encoding and the matching.

The event switches by date: the build decides upcoming or past, and a small inline
script checks again in the browser, so after 17:00 on 14 November the registration
box gives way to a "took place" note even if the site is not rebuilt. A build after
the date leaves the registration box, and the encoded number, out of the HTML.

The page content lives in one component so the event facts cannot drift between the
three languages. The nl and fr /communities copies had a closing sentence spliced into
the middle of another; that text is replaced by the new card. Eyebrows use a comma
instead of a middot.
